answer: Slew-rate-limited influence resists sybils: an identity's weight may rise by at most a fixed small increment per epoch, regardless of activity volume, so standing is gated by real calendar time, not burst volume. A swarm minted today cannot buy instant weight — every fake is throttled to the same gentle ramp, and high influence takes many epochs of survival each. Like a gale that cannot fill an inlet faster than its narrow mouth admits, concentrated effort cannot convert to sudden standing. The atlas of fakes must each wait out that same slow climb; no parallel spend shortens it.
